claims.quote: The voice of another aerocab driver hailing them made them realize that there were still ties that bound them to Earth
claims.description: Flying taxis (aerocabs) carry passengers along busy airways and land on rooftops.

claims.quote: Ralph had immediately transmitted the lost girl's photograph to the Central Office where it was placed before a Telephot connecting with every member of the entire police force, and the picture was reproduced for them in their portable radio instruments for ten seconds
claims.description: A missing person's photo is broadcast instantly to every police officer's portable radio picture device.

claims.quote: with strict orders to record every message, to tune into everything, and to take the messages down on the recorder discs.
claims.description: Incoming radio messages are recorded automatically on recording discs.

claims.quote: As all space flyers must be licensed by law, he had no trouble in getting the information he desired.
claims.description: Spacecraft must be licensed and registered with the authorities, like cars.

claims.quote: A new machine of a well-known Detroit firm had been registered four days ago, and the description of the owner answered to that of Fernand 60O 10.
claims.description: Private spacecraft are built and sold by commercial manufacturers to individual buyers.

claims.quote: the only machine out in the universe made with Magnelium
claims.description: A newly invented metal, Magnelium, is used for spacecraft hulls.

claims.quote: From the intensity and the elapsed time of the reflected impulses, the distance between the earth and the flyer can then be accurately and quickly calculated.
claims.description: Spacecraft are located by beaming waves at them and timing the reflections (radar), which also identify the metal they are made of.

claims.quote: He found that Fernand's machine at that time was about 400,000 miles distant from the earth and apparently headed in the direction of the planet Venus.
claims.description: Private spacecraft fly between planets at tens of thousands of miles an hour.

claims.quote: As Planet Governor it is my duty to advise you that you have not the right to place your person in unnecessary danger.
claims.description: Earth is governed by a single Planet Governor.

claims.quote: Allow me furthermore to point out to you that under the law "+" scientists are not allowed to endanger their lives under any circumstances.
claims.description: Law forbids top-ranked scientists from risking their lives.

claims.quote: The official took the proffered hand, and no sooner had he grasped it than he stiffened and became as rigid as stone.
claims.description: A drug (Catalepsol) delivered by a pinprick paralyzes a person for about fifteen minutes.

claims.quote: Towards the end of the twenty-first century, when atmospheric flying had become common, scientists began seriously to think of constructing machinery to enable man to leave the confines of the planet to which humanity had been chained for ages.
claims.description: Air travel becomes commonplace and scientists begin planning space travel.
claims.stated_time: Towards the end of the twenty-first century

claims.quote: Towards the beginning of the twenty-second century economic conditions had become acute and the enormous population of Earth, which had passed the twelve billion mark, clamored for an adequate outlet which the planet itself could no longer furnish.
claims.description: Earth's population passes twelve billion and overpopulation creates pressure to expand into space.
claims.stated_time: Towards the beginning of the twenty-second century

claims.quote: it was equally well known that Earth's scientists and engineers felt that they could, in a few years' time, make it habitable.
claims.description: Engineers expect to make the airless moon habitable (terraforming).

claims.quote: This scientist had made extensive studies of the gyroscope and had finally evolved a machine which when set in motion would rise freely and continue to rise as long as power was supplied.
claims.description: A gyroscopic anti-gravity machine, electrically driven, overcomes gravity; 12 kg of it can lift 1,000 kg.

claims.quote: Space flyers were equipped with from six to twelve large anti-gravitators attached to various points of their shells, all of which could be worked in unison, or operated independently in order to control the direction of the flyer.
claims.description: Spacecraft are steered by several anti-gravity units that can be run together or separately.

claims.quote: in spite of the fact that the machine had triple walls, the spaces between being filled with poor heat conducting materials.
claims.description: Spacecraft have triple insulated walls against heat from atmospheric friction and the cold of space.

claims.quote: The general aspect of the Earth as seen from Ralph's flyer was that of a delicate faint blue green ball with white caps at each of the poles.
claims.description: From space, Earth looks like a faint blue-green ball with white polar caps against a black sky.

claims.quote: The stars shone with a brilliancy never seen from Earth; distant constellations which ordinarily cannot be seen, except, with a telescope, were plainly visible to him, in outer space.
claims.description: Outside the atmosphere the stars shine far brighter and faint stars become visible to the naked eye.

claims.quote: Had he held his hand against the glass window of the space flyer where the sun could strike it full, his hand would have been burned in a few seconds.
claims.description: Unfiltered sunlight in space is hot enough to burn a hand through a window in seconds.

claims.quote: Inside of a space flyer, which had an infinitely small gravity, objects weighed practically nothing.
claims.description: Objects inside a spacecraft are weightless and float freely.

claims.quote: The passenger in a flyer could perform an incredible amount of work without tiring and without effort.
claims.description: Weightlessness lets people work for long periods without tiring.

claims.quote: Sleep was practically impossible.
claims.description: In weightlessness people hardly need or manage to sleep, because nothing tires them.

claims.quote: The sun heated one-half of the flyer's shell to a fierce heat, but the side turned away from the sun was exposed to the terrible stellar cold (absolute zero) and a fairly comfortable temperature was the result.
claims.description: A spacecraft's sunlit and shaded sides balance to a comfortable cabin temperature inside Mars's orbit.

claims.quote: The air supply was manufactured by chemical means on board, but very little was needed, as the original supply taken from the earth is used over and over by altering the carbonic acid gas by means of automatic generators.
claims.description: Spacecraft recycle their air, chemically converting exhaled carbon dioxide with automatic generators.

claims.quote: If the flyer were brought to this point its gyroscopes could be at rest, as the machine would not be attracted by either body.
claims.description: A spacecraft parked at the neutral point between two bodies needs no power and would orbit the sun like a tiny planet.

claims.quote: A hissing sound was heard, and Fernand was seen to fall backwards, the window turning green at the same moment.
claims.description: A ray weapon (the Radioperforer) stuns a person through a window.

claims.quote: He then pushed the connecting tube of his flyer into the tube-joint of Fernand's machine.
claims.description: Two spacecraft are held together by an electromagnet and joined by an airtight tube so a person can cross between them (docking).

claims.quote: Kneeling by his side Ralph applied a small electrical shocking device to the spine of the insensible man, with the result that in a few minutes Fernand opened his eyes and stared dazedly into those of his captor.
claims.description: A small electric shock device applied to the spine revives an unconscious person.

claims.quote: I found myself gripped by Llysanorh', the Martian, and I might as well have fought a tiger as that seven-footer.
claims.description: Seven-foot-tall Martians live among and travel with Earth people.

claims.quote: Surely, not to Venus where the inhabitants were nearly all Terrestrials, and whose laws were identical with those of Earth.
claims.description: Venus has been colonized by people from Earth and is governed by Earth's laws.

claims.quote: They would not be permitted to live on Mars, neither would Earth or Venus accept them.
claims.description: Planetary laws bar a Martian and an Earth woman from settling together on Mars, Earth or Venus.
